body.statement: For every optimal support cell and every replacement atom in the same arm, \(\phi_{at}\ge\phi_{as}+g(z_{at}-z_{as})\) for each \(g\in G_{as}\). Hence, if \(z_{as}<z_{at}\), every \(g\in G_{as}\) and \(h\in G_{at}\) obey \(g\le[\phi_{at}-\phi_{as}]/[z_{at}-z_{as}]\le h\). The intervals \(I_{as}\) are strictly ordered and disjoint within each arm. If \(I_{as}\) and \(I_{at}\) lie in one interval of length \(H\), then \(|z_{at}-z_{as}|\le H\) and \(0\le\phi_{at}-\phi_{as}-g(z_{at}-z_{as})\le H^2\), including ties and dyadic-boundary contacts under the singleton convention.
body.justification: The ordered slope interval is the cost-specific mechanism that makes multiscale repair quadratic rather than merely Lipschitz.
body.gap: Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025, Lemma on finite-support optimal couplings) use coordinate exchanges to bound support sums; they do not derive ordered scalar dual intervals or an integer-repair modulus.
body.consumer: The interval geometry supplies the summable per-scale charge in the deterministic rounding algorithm.
